abstract: Post-transcriptional modifications near the anticodon of transfer ribonucleic acids (tRNAs) ensure translation fidelity and accuracy. For instance, at position 37, the universally conserved and essential nucleoside N6-threonylcarbamoyladenosine (t6A) supports decoding of ANN triplets. In some organisms t6A is converted to cyclic t6A (ct6A), but only little is known about this ATP-dependent reaction and the corresponding threonylcarbamoyladenosine dehydratases (Tcds). We here show that yeast Tcds localize to the outer mitochondrial membrane and co-purify with tRNAs recognizing ANN codons. Depending on the number of TCD genes in the genome, the proteins form V-shaped hetero- or homodimers, of which at least one subunit binds and modifies tRNAs. The C-terminal, monomeric domain shares similarities with Cas9-endonucleases and assists tRNA recognition, while the N-terminal domain mediates dimerization and contains the active site. Structure-based mutagenesis and activity assays imply that yeast Tcds lack a catalytic cysteine and do not covalently bind their substrate as proposed for Escherichia coli TcdA.
